rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth reading of wasat makes the community religiously moderate between excess and negligence, unlike Christian exaggeration and Jewish shortcomings.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكونوا وسطا على معنى أنهم متوسطون في الدين بين المفرط والمفرط والغالي والمقصر في الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported interpretations of wasat are close and can coexist.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الأقوال متقاربة غير متنافية والله أعلم

rows.speaker: الأصحاب
rows.claim: The Ashab argue that God creates human acts: the community's justice and goodness are expressly attributed to God's making and creation.
rows.anchor: دالة على أن عدالة هذه الأمة وخيريتهم بجعل الله وخلقه وهذا صريح في المذهب

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila interpret God's making as providing gracious aids that lead this community to choose right in speech and deed.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : المراد من هذا الجعل فعل الألطاف التي علم الله تعالى أنه متى فعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ashab reject the Mu'tazili reading as abandoning the verse's apparent sense without a necessity to do so.
rows.anchor: أن هذا ترك للظاهر وذلك مما لا يصار إليه إلا عند قيام الدلائل على أنه لا يمكن حمل الآية على ظاهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding promise that God guides whom He wills supports the Ashab's view that God selectively grants guidance, reinforcing this verse.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى قال قبل هذه الآية : { يهدى من يشآء إلى صراط مستقيم } ( البقرة : 142 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has already given everyone all gracious aids within His power, so such aids cannot explain why believers alone are singled out.
rows.anchor: كل ما في مقدور الله تعالى من الألطاف في حق الكل فقد فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obligatory gracious aid cannot be an act of favor, whereas this verse presents God's making as a favor to the community.
rows.anchor: فعل اللطف واجب والواجب لا يجوز ذكره في معرض الامتنان

rows.speaker: جمهور الأصحاب وجمهور المعتزلة
rows.claim: Most Ashab and most Mu'tazila infer that communal consensus is authoritative: God calls the community just and good, so it cannot collectively agree on a prohibited act.
rows.anchor: احتج جمهور الأصحاب وجمهور المعتزلة بهذه الآية على أن إجماع الأمة حجة

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: An objector says the verse cannot apply literally to every individual, since some community members are plainly unjust, and proposes the infallible Imams instead.
rows.anchor: وصف الأمة بالعدالة يقتضي اتصاف كل واحد / منهم بها وخلاف ذلك معلوم بالضرورة

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: Even if the verse is literal, an objector denies that wasat necessarily means the best or most virtuous.
rows.anchor: سلمنا أنها ليست متروكة الظاهرة لكن لا نسلم أن الوسط من كل شيء خياره

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: Justice consists in human performance of duties and avoidance of sins, while God is said to make the community wasat; identifying these would make one act have two agents.
rows.anchor: أن عدالة الرجل عبارة عن أداء الواجبات واجتناب المحرمات وهذا من فعل العبد

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: Wasat literally means something midway between two things; making it mean justice and goodness would create lexical equivocation.
rows.anchor: فجعله حقيقة في العدالة والخيرية يقتضي الاشتراك وهو خلال الأصل

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: An objector allows that the community may be good merely by avoiding major sins, leaving open the possibility that its consensus includes minor errors.
rows.anchor: سلمنا اتصافهم بالخيرية ولكن لم لا يكفي في حصول هذا الوصف الاجتناب عن الكبائر فقط

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: The objector adds that committing minor sins does not invalidate testimony, so it need not undermine the community's goodness as witnesses.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى حكم بكونهم عدولا ليكونوا شهداء على الناس وفعل الصغائر لا يمنع الشهادة

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: Even if the community avoids both major and minor sins, that justice may only be required when it gives testimony in the afterlife, not during worldly life.
rows.anchor: عدالة الشهود إنما تعتبر حالة الأداء لا حالة التحمل

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: The objector argues that the address may concern only people alive at revelation; their consensus would not establish the authority of later generations.
rows.anchor: المخاطبين بهذا الخطاب هم الذين كانوا موجودين عند نزول هذه الآية لأن الخطاب مع من لم يوجد محال

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: If consensus is limited to the first generation, it is unusable unless every person, their survival past the Prophet, and their agreement are all identified, which is nearly impossible.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ذلك كالمتعذر امتنع التمسك بالإجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that the community is just in matters on which it agrees; when members disagree, they may commit error, since the address concerns them collectively.
rows.anchor: جعل كل واحد منهم عند اجتماعه مع غيره بهذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if not every individual is just, the verse's general rule remains valid for the qualified members; because they are unidentified, their agreement is needed to ensure they are included.
rows.anchor: بل المراد أنه لا بد وأن يوجد فيما بينهم من يكون بهذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi illustrates this with a family in which one son must be right: unanimous agreement reveals the correct view, but agreement by all except one cannot, since the dissenter may be right.
rows.anchor: إذا لم نعلمه بعينه ووجدنا أولاده مجتمعين على رأي علمناه حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi accepts the implication that the human act is created by God, as argued earlier.
rows.anchor: هذا مذهبنا على ما تقدم بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He initially argues that God's truthful declaration of the community's goodness rules out minor sin, since a minor sin is not good.
rows.anchor: حصول المخبر عنه ، وفعل الصغيرة ليس بخير

rows.speaker: لقائل
rows.claim: A critic replies that calling someone good can mean good in some respects only, not in every matter, so the verse does not exclude major or minor sins; Razi admits this objection challenges his proof.
rows.anchor: الإخبار عن الشخص بأنه خير أعم من الإخبار عنه بأنه خير في جميع الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi had defended this inference in legal theory, but acknowledges that the objection applies to it.
rows.anchor: وكنا قد نصرنا هذه الدلالة في أصول الفقه إلا أن هذا السؤال وارد عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that the address encompasses the entire community from its earliest members through those who come after them until the Hour, as do obligations of retaliation and fasting.
rows.anchor: خطاب لجميع الأمة أولها وآخرها ، من كان منهم موجودا وقت نزول هذه الآية

rows.speaker: معترض
rows.claim: An objection asks how an address to all generations jointly establishes the justice of each era's community and makes it authoritative for those after it.
rows.anchor: لو كان الأمر كذلك لكان هذا خطابا لجميع من يوجد إلى قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the community is to bear witness over people, the verse must authorize each era; otherwise no one would remain after the whole community ended for it to witness against.
rows.anchor: لأنه تعالى لما جعلهم شهداء على الناس ، فلو اعتبرنا أول الأمة وآخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each era's people may be called an ummah, a group oriented toward one direction; the indefinite phrase ummatan wasatan also encompasses each era.
rows.anchor: فإن الأمة اسم للجماعة التي تؤم جهة واحدة ، ولا شك أن أهل كل عصر كذلك

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most interpreters say the community's testimony occurs in the afterlife: it testifies for prophets whom their peoples deny, and Muhammad then certifies his community's justice; Razi links this to 4:41.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الأمة تشهد للأنبياء على أنهم الذين يكذبونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says peoples deny that prophets conveyed their message; Muhammad's community testifies from God's Book, after which Muhammad is asked about and certifies them.
rows.anchor: روي أن الأمم يجحدون تبليغ الأنبياء

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi objects that this report depends on people lying at the Resurrection, which he considers impossible.
rows.anchor: أن أهل القيامة قد يكذبون ، وهذا باطل عند القاضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi defers discussion of whether people may lie at the Resurrection to his commentary on 6:23–24.
rows.anchor: سنتكلم على هذه المسألة في سورة الأنعام في تفسير قوله تعالى : { ثم لم تكن فتنتهم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi asks why God does not testify directly, since both the community's and the Messenger's afterlife testimony ultimately rests on God's testimony to the prophets.
rows.anchor: شهادة الأمة وشهادة الرسول مستندة في الآخرة إلى شهادة الله تعالى على صدق الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that the testimony displays Muhammad's community's special merit: its prompt belief in God and all prophets makes it like the just among the sinful, so its testimony is accepted against other nations but theirs is not against it.
rows.anchor: الحكمة في ذلك تمييز أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في الفضل عن سائر الأمم بالمبادرة إلى تصديق الله تعالى وتصديق جميع الأنبياء

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi objects that reports of this kind do not count as testimony.
rows.anchor: مثل هذه الأخبار لا تسمى شهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls that objection weak: the Prophet permits testimony when something is known as clearly as the sun, and revelation is known that clearly.
rows.anchor: والشيء الذي أخبر الله تعالى عنه فهو معلوم مثل الشمس فوجب جواز الشهادة عليه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the verse to mean that the community testifies against people for deeds in which they opposed the truth.
rows.anchor: لتشهدوا على الناس بأعمالهم التي خالفوا الحق فيها قال ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The first class of witnesses is the angels assigned to record human deeds, as in the verses about each soul's driver and witness, the ever-present recorder, and noble recording guardians.
rows.anchor: الملائكة الموكلون بإثبات أعمال العباد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The second class is the prophets: Jesus witnesses over his people during his life, while Muhammad is witness over his community and the nations.
rows.anchor: { وكنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم فلما توفيتنى كنت أنت الرقيب عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The third class is the special testimony of Muhammad's community, also mentioned among the witnesses and on the Day the witnesses arise.
rows.anchor: شهادة أمة محمد خاصة . قال تعالى : { وجىء بالنبيين والشهداء }

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The fourth class is testimony by bodily organs, comparable to or even more striking than a person's own admission.
rows.anchor: شهادة الجوارح وهي بمنزلة الإقرار بل أعجب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic root of testimony centers on seeing: witnessing and observation mean sight, while knowledge in the heart is called seeing because the two are closely related.
rows.anchor: الشهادة والمشاهدة والشهود هو الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By extension, knowledge and its knower, evidence, and an informant can all be called witnessing or a witness because they disclose a thing.
rows.anchor: والعارف بالشيء : شاهدا ومشاهدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal usage, witness becomes a technical term for one who reports people's rights in specified wording and specified circumstances.
rows.anchor: ثم اختص هذا اللفظ في عرف الشرع بمن يخبر عن حقوق الناس بألفاظ مخصوصة على جهات مخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More broadly, anyone who knows the state of a thing and discloses it is a witness over it.
rows.anchor: إن كل من عرف حال شيء وكشف عنه كان شاهدا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's witnesses must serve in worldly life: God says He made the community just so it could witness, and the past-tense making applies at least in the present.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى جعلهم عدولا في الدنيا لأجل أن يكونوا شهداء وذلك يقتضي أن يكونوا شهداء في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse links being wasat to being witnesses as consequence to condition, so worldly justice entails worldly testimony.
rows.anchor: رتب كونهم شهداء على صيرورتهم وسطا ترتيب الجزاء على الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relevant testimony is performance, not merely bearing witness: justice is required for giving testimony, not for carrying it until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: الشهادة المعتبرة في الآية لا التحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the whole community testifies to something in worldly life, its statement is authoritative; this is what the authority of consensus means.
rows.anchor: مؤدين للشهادة في دار الدنيا ، وذلك يقتضي أن يكون مجموع الأمة إذا أخبروا عن شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly testimony does not rule out the community also testifying in the afterlife as reported: it first identifies accepters and rejecters, then testifies to them before God.
rows.anchor: لا يبطل القولين الأولين لأنا بينا بهذه الدلالة أن الأمة لا بد وأن يكونوا شهودا في الدنيا وهذا لا ينافي كونهم شهودا في القيامة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is a witness in the sense of one who performs and explains testimony; worldly consensus reveals truth, and the community can later testify about those who accepted or rejected it.
rows.anchor: يعني مؤديا ومبينا ، ثم لا يمتنع أن تحصل مع ذلك لهم الشهادة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People whose disbelief or flagrant sin is evident—including anthropomorphists, Kharijites, and Rafidites—do not count toward consensus, whether their error is in belief or action, rejection of a text, or interpretation.
rows.anchor: من ظهر كفره وفسقه نحو المشبهة والخوارج والروافض فإنه لا يعتد به في الإجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only people characterized by justice and goodness can be witnesses, which explains why manifest unbelief or sin excludes a person.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى إنما جعل الشهداء من وصفهم بالعدالة والخيرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says witnesses are over people rather than for them because their statement or action imposes an obligation, which is against them in the present life.
rows.anchor: لأن قولهم يقتضي التكليف إما بقول وإما بفعل وذلك عليه لا له في الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause emphasizes testimony over the nations; the later clause singles out the Messenger as witness over the community.
rows.anchor: لأن الغرض في الأول إثبات شهادتهم على الأمم وفي الآخر الاختصاص بكون الرسول شهيدا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ja'alna means legislated or prescribed, as when God says He did not make bahira, meaning He did not prescribe it as religion.
rows.anchor: معناه ما شرعنا وما حكمنا كقوله : { ما جعل الله من بحيرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kunta alayha means that the Prophet believed in facing that direction, like the expression that one person had a debt against another.
rows.anchor: أي كنت معتقدا لاستقبالها ، كقول القائل : كان لفلان على فلان دين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the relative clause is not an adjective of qibla; it fills the second object slot of ja'alna.
rows.anchor: ليس بصفة للقبلة ، إنما هو ثاني مفعولي جعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading explains the prior qibla as the Kaaba: the Prophet prayed toward it in Mecca, then Jerusalem after migration to conciliate the Jews, and God returned him to it as a test.
rows.anchor: كان يصلي بمكة إلى الكعبة ثم أمر بالصلاة إلى بيت المقدس بعد الهجرة تأليفا لليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading takes Jerusalem as the qibla God had previously assigned: the original command was to face the Kaaba, and Jerusalem was a temporary test of who would follow the Messenger.
rows.anchor: استقبالك بيت المقدس كان أمرا عارضا لغرض

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says that without transmitted reports the verse does not identify the earlier qibla; kuntum can mean became, as in 3:110, or always was, as in 4:158, allowing the Kaaba to be intended.
rows.anchor: ذكره أبو مسلم فقال : لولا الروايات لم تدل الآية على قبلة من قبل الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-na'lama is purposive; whether God can have an objective and how to interpret the phrase if not was discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: لام الغرض والكلام في أنه هل يصح الغرض على الله أو لا يصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording seems to imply that God did not know beforehand and changed the qibla to acquire knowledge; the same difficulty appears in several other verses.
rows.anchor: يوهم أن العلم بذلك الشيء لم يكن حاصلا فهو فعل ذلك الفعل ليحصل له ذلك العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation means that God's party—prophets and believers—will know, as when a king says we conquered a city to mean his allies conquered it.
rows.anchor: ليعلم حزبنا من النبيين والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom is illustrated by saying that Umar conquered the Sawad.
rows.anchor: ومنه يقال : فتح عمر السواد

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: A divine report narrated by the Prophet says God speaks of a servant who failed to lend to Him and insulted Him by cursing time.
rows.anchor: فيما يحكيه عن ربه : ( استقرضت عبدي فلم يقرضني ، وشتمني

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Another Prophetic saying equates an offense against God's protected friend with an offense against God, illustrating attribution through a follower.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( من أهان لي وليا فقد أهانني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is that the event makes what was nonexistent come into existence, so God knows the person as existing; interpreters disagree whether prior knowledge of future existence is knowledge of its existence when realized.
rows.anchor: ليحصل المعدوم فيصير موجودا ، فقوله : { إلا لنعلم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes knowing to mean distinguishing sincere believers from hypocrites by exposing their hearts, allowing believers to know whom to befriend and avoid.
rows.anchor: إلا لنميز هؤلاء من هؤلاء بانكشاف ما في قلوبهم من الإخلاص والنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, distinction is called knowledge because it is one of knowledge's benefits and fruits.
rows.anchor: فسمي التمييز علما ، لأنه أحد فوائد العلم وثمراته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation makes na'lama mean see; Arabic can interchange knowledge, sight, and witnessing.
rows.anchor: العرب تضع العلم مكان الرؤية ، والرؤية مكان العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interchange of knowing and seeing is exemplified by Qur'anic expressions in 89:6, 105:1, and 14:19.
rows.anchor: كقوله : { ألم تر كيف } ( الفجر : 6 ) ( الفيل : 1 ) ( إبراهيم : 19 )

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reads the phrase as so that you may know, with the apparent first-person uncertainty transferred to the addressees, as in a debate staged to discover which disputant is ignorant.
rows.anchor: ما ذهب إليه الفراء : وهو أن حدوث العلم في هذه الآية راجع إلى المخاطبين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: This softened address attributes doubtful language to the speaker for gentleness, as in the phrase whether we or you are rightly guided.
rows.anchor: الاستمالة والرفق في الخطاب ، كقوله : { وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth interpretation says God treats people like an examiner who seems not to know, as justice requires.
rows.anchor: معاملة المختبر الذي كأنه لا يعلم ، إذ العدل يوجب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seventh interpretation treats knowledge as an extra particle: the phrase means only for followers to follow and turncoats to turn back, as in the idiom God did not know this from me for it did not happen.
rows.anchor: أن العلم صلة زائدة ، فقوله ؛ { إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب على عقبيه }

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: One view says the trial came from assigning a qibla: Arabs resented leaving the Kaaba for Jerusalem, then Jews resented the return to the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: فمن الناس من قال : إنما حصلت بسبب تعيين القبلة

rows.speaker: أكثرون من أهل التحقيق
rows.claim: Most critical scholars locate the trial in the change of qibla, when critics claimed Muhammad would not have changed his mind if certain.
rows.anchor: وأما الأكثرون من أهل التحقيق قالوا : هذه المحنة إنما حصلت بسبب التحويل

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal transmits from Ibn Jurayj that he had heard some people who had accepted Islam turn back, saying the direction changed from here to there.
rows.anchor: أنه قال : بلغني أنه رجع ناس ممن أسلم ، وقالوا مرة ههنا ومرة ههنا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that hypocrites questioned why the community abandoned its former qibla.
rows.anchor: فقال المنافقون : ما بالهم كانوا على قبلة ثم تركوها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that Muslims worried about the fate of fellow believers who had died praying toward Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: وقال المسلمون : لسنا نعلم حال إخواننا الذين ماتوا وهم يصلون نحو بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that some people thought Muhammad longed for the land of his father and birthplace.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : اشتاق إلى بلد أبيه ومولده

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that polytheists accused Muhammad of confusion in his religion.
rows.anchor: وقال المشركون : تحير في دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers the change-of-qibla explanation because the challenge of abrogation is greater than the challenge of the original qibla choice, matching God's description of the change as difficult except for the guided.
rows.anchor: هذا القول الأخير أولى لأن الشبهة في أمر النسخ أعظم من الشبهة الحاصلة بسبب تعيين القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning back on one's heels is a metaphor for disbelieving in God and His Messenger: abandoning faith and its proofs is like turning away from what lies ahead.
rows.anchor: استعارة ومعناه : من يكفر بالله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is another simile for turning away, as in the descriptions he turned away and became arrogant, and he denied and turned away.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { ثم أدبر واستكبر } ( المدثر : 23 ) وكما قال : { كذب وتولى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light kasra-form in has four uses: conditional, a lightened emphatic particle, negation, and an extra particle.
rows.anchor: أما قوله تعالى : { وإن كانت } ففيه مسائل : المسألة الأولى : ( إن ) المكسورة الخفيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conditional in links two clauses, with the condition as what entails and the response as what follows, as in if you come, I will honor you.
rows.anchor: فالمستلزم هو الشرط واللازم هو الجزاء كقولك : إن جئتني أكرمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightened emphatic in strengthens the clause like heavy in; it may precede a verb, and the following lām compensates for what was removed.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى : { إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ } ( الطارق : 4 ) وقال : { إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lightened emphatic form is distinguished from negative in, although both can be followed by nouns or verbs; the emphatic form takes a compensating lām.
rows.anchor: والفرق بينها وبين التي للجحد في قوله تعالى : { إن الكافرون إلا فى غرور }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negative in means not, as in the statements that judgment belongs only to God and people follow only conjecture, and that the two would not be held if they shifted.
rows.anchor: { إن الحكم إلا لله } ( الأنعام : 57 ) وقال : { إن تتبعون إلا الظن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra use of in adds no meaning, as in the idiom I did not see Zayd.
rows.anchor: وأما الرابعة وهي الزائدة فكقولك : ما إن رأيت زيدا
